title: Bridging the gap between patient needs and available services for effective treatment – investigating the transformation process of a large psychiatric care facility
summary:
A project is launching at ZfP Südwürttemberg, Reichenau, and PP.rt aimed at improving care for people with mental illnesses. It is called BEREIT! (“Needs-Based Development of Cross-Jurisdictional Care in the Psychiatric and Psychotherapeutic Transformation”). The project will run for five years.
The goal of the accompanying study, BEREIT. IMPACT is to capture and describe the potential changes for those involved and the contextual conditions over the course of this transformation project’s implementation at the system and stakeholder levels (patients, family members, staff). The study uses qualitative methods (interviews, group discussions, and participant observation) for this purpose. It is taking place in two selected care regions.
conditions: Patients receiving inpatient or outpatient general psychiatric treatment with the following primary diagnoses from the ICD-10 classification: F00–F09, F20 through F99

interventions.name: As examples of the overall transformation process, two regions providing comprehensive psychiatric care (Lake Constance District, Biberach District) will be studied at three measurement points over the course of the transformation process. Both regions include hospitals with general psychiatric ward

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients: The presence of a mental illness treated at the specified locations (in principle, all diagnoses except for a first diagnosis of substance use disorder; at least half of the patients must meet the criteria for a serious mental illness (SMI)), the ability to give informed consent, as well as sufficient German language skills and resilience to participate in an individual interview.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients: Primary substance use disorders (patients from the Lake Constance district are not treated there but are primarily referred to the specialized units at the ZfP Weissenau), lack of capacity to give informed consent, insufficient German language skills to conduct an interview, and insufficient resilience to handle an individual interview lasting approximately 45 minutes.
